name: Tirzah
title: Daughter of Zelophehad
summary: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad from the tribe of Manasseh. She and her sisters were known for bringing their case before Moses and the leaders of Israel, demanding inheritance rights to their deceased father's land since he had no sons. Their case led to an important law change in Israel that granted daughters inheritance rights when there were no male heirs.

keyEvents.title: Zelophehad's daughters bring their case before Moses
keyEvents.description: Tirzah and her four sisters stood before Moses, the priest Eleazar, the leaders, and the entire congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, demanding inheritance rights from their father, who had died in the wilderness without sons.

keyEvents.title: The Lord's ruling on the inheritance rights of daughters
keyEvents.description: The Lord told Moses that Zelophehad's daughters were right and should receive their father's property as an inheritance. This became a lasting law in Israel.

keyEvents.title: A new law on inheritance is established
keyEvents.description: Through the case of Tirzah and her sisters, a general law was enacted regarding inheritance when a man died without sons, securing property rights for women in Israel.

keyEvents.title: The question of marriage and tribal affiliation
keyEvents.description: The leaders of the tribe of Manasseh raised concern that the inheritance might pass to other tribes if daughters married outside their own tribe. It was therefore decided that inheriting daughters must marry within their own tribe.

keyEvents.title: Tirzah and her sisters marry within the tribe
keyEvents.description: Tirzah and her sisters obeyed the Lord's command and married men from the tribe of Manasseh, so that the inheritance remained within the tribe.

keyEvents.title: Tirzah is mentioned among Zelophehad's daughters during the land distribution
keyEvents.description: When the land of Canaan was distributed under Joshua, Zelophehad's daughters, including Tirzah, came forward and claimed their allotted inheritance as the Lord had commanded through Moses.
